items.text: The practice was three returns to the garden
“Anyone want to say one sentence about how that went — the garden visits, or what surfaced, or that you didn’t get to it?”
One sentence each, voluntary — received without commentary
“Good. The garden is still there. You can return any time. We continue.”
The whole scene, read slowly — the desperate father, the failed disciples, the boy in convulsions
He does not pretend the unbelief is not there — he names both at once. And Jesus does not rebuke him; Jesus heals the boy
The unbelief that is named and brought to Jesus is the unbelief that can be released; suppressed, it works as a quiet brake
Tonight is not generating new doubts — it is bringing the ones already there into the open, and bringing them to Jesus

panel.label: MARK 9:24
lines: “Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, ‘I believe; help my unbelief!’”

slides.title: The Any Doubts? Practice — Four Steps

items.text: NAME — the scripture, then the doubt. Specific, not abstract: “I doubt He hears prayer about this specific thing”
EXAGGERATE — make the doubt bigger, not smaller. You are not endorsing it; you are exposing it
SIT — what does the doubt feel like in your body? Ten or fifteen seconds. Don’t fix it. Feel it
RE-READ — your partner reads the same scripture again, slowly. The Spirit does the work; you do the noticing
Watch the demo — specific, honest, brief, and unresolved-but-honest is the gift

slides.title: Bridge to the Split — Parents First

items.text: Take the practice card (H11.1) — pairs form within your own family, a parent with their own teen
In every pair the parent goes first — arranged this week; nobody is being put on the spot tonight
“Teens: you go second, and you choose your own depth. A small doubt is enough. Passing is enough.”
No scripture in mind? H11.3 has examples — pick one with a flicker for you, not a hurricane
Partners: read, listen, re-read. Not fix. Not theologize. “We are not arguing the doubt. We are bringing it.”

slides.title: Any Doubts? in Pairs, within Families

items.text: Pick a scripture; your partner reads it slowly — from the physical Bible if possible
“What I notice is ___. The doubt I am holding is ___.” — specific
Exaggerate it, then sit with the feeling for 10–20 seconds
“Read it again, please.” Then: “What I notice this time is ___.”
The parent’s turn first, then switch — the teen at their own depth; pass-anytime holds
Two agreements: you are not arguing or fixing the doubt — and nothing leaves your pair
What happened in your pair stays in your pair — no one will be asked to share a doubt or a scripture
“One word about what the practice was like. Not the doubt — the practice.”
“Surprising.” “Heavy.” “Quiet.” “Awkward.” “Honest.” “Lighter.” Pass anytime
This practice fits in five minutes alone, or twenty with a friend — a way of bringing your real questions to God for the rest of your life
“The resolution is the Spirit’s work. The naming is yours. We do the naming. He does what only He can.”
Personal Doubts Inventory (H11.2) — twenty minutes with your journal, once this week
List 5–10 scriptures you say you believe; rate your honest trust, 1–5
For the two or three with the most hesitation — write the specific doubt, then sit with it
No shame. Just data. Yours alone — never turned in, never seen by the team
The Quarterly Pulse (H11.4) goes home tonight — three questions, five minutes, honest. Back in the bin at The Return’s door in January
Over the break: keep one practice alive — just one, your choice
